thread:
maya: quick RFC follow-up: prototype for a delegated observer service that can make local fallback decisions during canary/A-B rollouts. posting notes for ops + SRE review.
jon: sounds interesting — what's the main split vs central controller?
maya: central controller still owns rollout intents and global weights. observer's job is low-latency local mitigation: evict variant on a node, soft-degrade, or suggest routing hints. goal is avoid RTT to central for fast regressions.
alex: what signals does it use? infra only or model-eval too?
maya: infra (p95, 5xx), plus a small set of golden prompt evals per canary. we keep the evals lightweight (5-10 samples).
rachel: we need safeguards for flapping and noisy cohorts. how do you avoid oscillation?
maya: policy includes hysteresis, lease tokens per rollout-id, and majority agreement across N cohorts before global escalation. local mitigations can be immediate but are reversible by TTL.
jon: can you share the policy schema you prototyped?
maya: sure, short example we used in staging (pseudo-JSON shown inline):
```
rollout_id: r-2026-03-21-42
signals:
  - name: latency_p95
    threshold_ms: 1200
    window_s: 60
    hysteresis_s: 30
  - name: error_rate
    threshold_pct: 0.5
    window_s: 120
action:
  local: route_fallback
  global_escalate_after: 3
```
alex: route_fallback meaning proxy sends new sessions to baseline locally? what about cache/prefix state?
rachel: prefer soft routing for new sessions to avoid cold KV-cache misses. fallback should try to preserve prefix cache where possible.
maya: agreed. observer returns decisions via /v1/decision -> {action, reason, ttl}. proxies poll every 5s and apply hints. TTL key so proxies auto-revert if observer disappears.
jon: decision lineage/observability is critical. tracers, ids?
maya: observer attaches decision_id header for a time window. console will link decision_id -> signals -> cohort votes. metrics: decisions/sec, avg_ttl, rollback_count.
sre-lead: ops constraint: opt-out per namespace/customer. some customers want central-only control for compliance.
jon: conflict resolution? central controller override path?
maya: central controller can post a cancel token or veto; absent veto observer decisions stand for TTL. observer is configured per rollout to be advisory or active.
alex: failure modes? if observer crashes do we default to rollback or central-only?
maya: fail-open to central-only (i.e., no automatic local fallback). we must not auto-evict on observer failure.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: observer v0.3 -> staging eu-west-1 (build 20260321.85).
rachel: request: add an advisory debug mode where observer only suggests actions (no apply) so we can run non-invasive for 1 week.
maya: plan: advisory at 10% of canaries for one week, then active for those cohorts if stable.
jon: can we get a short oncall runbook blurb? how to revert observer decisions and follow decision trace?
maya: will draft runbook: quick steps -> 1) cancel decision via controller token 2) clear observer lease 3) instruct proxies to clear route hints 4) consult decision_id in console for signal history. i'll post follow-up.
sre-lead: also ensure metric alert thresholds for observer health (heartbeat, decision-rate) and a kill-switch flag to opt-out cluster-wide.
maya: noted. next steps: finalize policy schema, add provenance headers, implement advisory mode, and share runbook. thanks all :thumbsup:
